articles.title_orig: Japan defense chief vows to boost monitoring after sailing of China carrier
articles.title_zh: Japan defense chief vows to boost monitoring after sailing of China carrier
articles.content_orig:
TOKYO - Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said enhancing the country's defense posture in the Pacific is an "urgent" task, including for information gathering and surveillance, after the recent sailing of the Chinese aircraft carrier Liaoning in waters off Okinawa.
Koizumi said the carrier's movement was part of efforts by China "to improve the operational capability of aircraft carriers and enhance its ability to conduct operations in distant maritime and aerial areas" as it "increasingly expands military activities around Japan."
The Liaoning, accompanied by several destroyers, sailed between the Okinawa main island and Miyako Island in the southern Japan prefecture on Wednesday as it headed from the East China Sea toward the Pacific, with carrier-borne aircraft seen taking off and landing around 10 times, the ministry said.
Japan's Self-Defense Forces responded by dispatching a destroyer and two patrol aircraft, and scrambling fighter aircraft, the ministry said. The aircraft carrier sailed toward the South China Sea on Thursday, it said.
The Chinese navy has said that the dispatch of the Liaoning, one of the country's three aircraft carriers, to the Western Pacific for an exercise was in line with an "annual routine training plan."

articles.title_orig: 3 children, 1 teacher killed in shooting at Bend, Oregon, elementary school, police say; suspect dead
articles.title_zh: 3 children, 1 teacher killed in shooting at Bend, Oregon, elementary school, police say; suspect dead
articles.content_orig:
Three children and a teacher were killed, and two others critically wounded, in a shooting on Thursday at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, authorities said.
The suspect, a 16-year-old male, was shot and killed by a bystander, Bend police said.
Along with the teacher, the three children killed were ages 5, 8 and 11, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said in a news conference Thursday night. Two others, a 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher, were taken to St. Charles Medical Center   with critical injuries. No names were immediately released.
Krantz said that officers were called to the school just before 1 p.m. on a 911 call from a person who said they had been shot at several times while in their vehicle by a suspect with a long gun. Emergency dispatchers then received dozens of 911 calls that the suspect had entered the school.
The shooter forced his way into the school by "shooting at locked doors," Krantz said.
When officers arrived at the school within three minutes of the first 911 call, they discovered that the suspect had been killed by a bystander, Krantz said.
"An officer reported that the suspect had been shot by a community member who had seen the suspect enter the school and pursued him into the school and engaged him," Krantz told reporters.
After officers entered the building, Krantz said, they found the four deceased victims.
Officials would not say exactly what type of weapon was used in the attack or how many rounds were fired. Multiple law enforcement sources told CBS News the suspect used a shotgun.
There was no word on a motive. Police could also not say if the suspect had a connection to the school. No details were provided on the bystander who shot and killed the suspect.
Authorities evacuated the school and transported all students and staff to a nearby church where they could be reunited with their families, Krantz said.
"Today an unthinkable tragedy happened at Silver Rail Elementary School," Bend-La Pine Superintendent Steven Cook said in the news conference. "No community should have to do what we are doing right now. I don't have any words for what this community is feeling right now."
FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency's local office was on scene and assisting local law enforcement. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives was also on scene to assist local authorities, including the Oregon State Police, a law enforcement source said.
Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek praised the bystander who "heroically intervened to stop further loss of life," saying the person's actions carry "a heavy emotional burden."
"All Oregonians mourn this loss today," Kotek said in the news briefing. "This is a horrible day. No parent should have to have this kind of day. And no community should have to live through this kind of day."
Bend-La Pine Schools said that all schools in the district would be canceling classes and athletic events on Friday due to the shooting.
Bend is located in central Oregon, about 150 miles southeast of Portland.
Last year there were 235 shooting incidents at K-12 schools in the U.S., according to data from the K-12 School Shooting Database . So far this year, there have been at least 149, including the one in Bend, Oregon. While still higher than pre-pandemic levels, school shooting incidents appear to be decreasing from a peak in 2023.
Grace  Manthey contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine abandons truce and attacks Russian oil refinery as Zelenskyy says he feels betrayed by Trump
articles.title_zh: Ukraine abandons truce and attacks Russian oil refinery as Zelenskyy says he feels betrayed by Trump
articles.content_orig:
Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham says goodbye to Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy after their meeting at 10 Downing Street in London, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. Alberto Pezzali/AP hide caption
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian drones attacked a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region early Thursday, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that a brief truce spurned by Moscow was over amid deepening tensions with Washington.
The drone strike started a fire at the refinery about 300 kilometers (180 miles) southeast of Moscow, Russia's Defense Ministry and Ryazan Gov. Pavel Malkov said. Russia's Astra online news outlet posted what it said was a photograph of the blaze.
A senior Ukrainian official who spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorized to speak publicly confirmed that Ukraine had hit the refinery.
The strike could further complicate Kyiv's relations with U.S. President Donald Trump, which have soured again in recent days.
Zelenskyy was outraged by Russia's continuing aerial bombardment of his country's energy infrastructure in apparent defiance of Trump's demand on Sunday for both sides to halt those attacks. The Ukrainian government said that it was heeding the ceasefire.
Zelenskyy complained that, despite going along with Trump's demand for a truce, Ukraine in recent days was denied the usual Western intelligence on Russian ballistic missile strikes and limits were placed on its use of U.S.-made Starlink communication terminals.
The Ukrainian leader said that his patience had run out. He said in an interview with the Financial Times published Thursday that Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries would resume. "We're done," he was quoted as saying.
Trump made a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel, despite international efforts to sanction Russia for its invasion and diplomatically isolate Putin.
Zelenskyy slammed the agreement, saying it would allow Russia to press on with its full-scale invasion of Ukraine that began more than 4½ years ago. U.S. efforts under Trump to end the war have made no progress.
Zelenskyy said in an interview late Wednesday with Piers Morgan on the British journalist's YouTube show that he felt betrayed by Trump's deal with Putin, the energy ceasefire announcement and the Starlink operational issues.
"Really, yes, between us," Zelenskyy told Morgan when asked if he felt betrayed by the American president. "Our country has to survive, and we count on our real partners, strategic partners, the United States and President Trump."
He said that the U.S. behavior "was really strange and what was not like between partners but that they switch off Starlink, so some actually crazy steps between us."
In the same interview, Zelenskyy said that "we are losing a strong partner" in the United States.
He said that "it's painful when President Trump chooses one side, not our side. But we are OK that he's in the middle."
Zelenskyy said someone is pushing Trump into a stance that is "not the right side of history."
The Starlink speed limits choked Ukrainian efforts to defend itself and hit back against Russia, Kyiv officials said.
Elon Musk noted on X that the military version of Starlink is controlled by the U.S. military and Trump.
The absence of Western intelligence leaves Ukraine more vulnerable to Russian ballistic missiles. Trump has said the U.S. hasn't stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine.
Three people were killed and six others injured after the Kirovohrad region of central Ukraine came under a Russian drone attack lasting more than 10 hours, Ukraine's Emergency Services said Thursday.
Zelenskyy said on X that between midnight and Thursday morning Russia launched more than 850 drones at Ukraine, adding that the barrage came "precisely at a time when the speed of our defensive capabilities is being artificially restricted."
Russian aerial attacks hit 15 Ukrainian regions, he said.
"It is obvious that Russia deliberately chose to escalate its attacks after receiving sanctions relief and seeing attempts to pressure Ukraine," Zelenskyy said. "It is important that everyone in America stand not with the aggressor, but with our efforts to protect lives, end this war and guarantee security."
Ukrainian air defenses stopped 536 Russian drones during a large-scale overnight attack, the Ukrainian Air Force said, but impacts were recorded at 31 locations.
Russia's Defense Ministry said that air defenses downed 166 Ukrainian drones overnight. It said that its forces hit two vessels carrying military cargo.

articles.title_orig: The Tesla Roadster flew, drove upside down, and hit 60mph in under a second
articles.title_zh: The Tesla Roadster flew, drove upside down, and hit 60mph in under a second
articles.content_orig:
Tesla showed off its long-delayed next-generation Roadster on Thursday, almost a decade after Elon Musk's company started taking deposits for the electric sports car.
The event was livestreamed from a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, near Waco, starting at 7:55 p.m. local time, or 8:55 p.m. ET. In attendance along with Musk were design leader Franz von Holzhausen and Lars Moravy, vice president of vehicle engineering.
"You're going to see some crazy stuff tonight," Musk said. "You're going to see the results of what happens when you have a collaboration with the world's best car company and the world's best rocket company."
Tesla's original Roadster, designed and engineered by a team led by founding CEO Martin Eberhard, was based on a Lotus Elise chassis and was first delivered in 2008, selling for roughly $100,000 in small volumes until 2012.
The next-generation Roadster is expected to be a high-end, low-volume model that relies on SpaceX technology, such as cold gas thrusters, to enable it to hover. Musk fanatics have been gearing up for the demonstration, expressing their excitement on social media, but the Roadster isn't likely to have any material financial impact on the company.
At the event, Musk and his team showcased a white sports car that raced up a curved ramp, then hung upside down and vaulted off it, flipping in mid-air and hovering slowly before landing on the ground.
The two-seater can go from zero to 60 miles per hour in under a second, according to Tesla's timer, a feat Moravy demonstrated for the live audience.
Musk said the next-generation Roadster would enter production in 2028. The price wasn't announced.
Tesla reopened reservations for the refreshed Roadster in recent weeks, accepting $50,000 deposits from prospective buyers in the U.S., Canada and China. Executives are expected to disclose specific pricing, details and production targets.
Musk first promoted the refreshed Roadster concept at an event in November 2017 , and the following June in a series of tweets. He wrote at that time, "SpaceX option package for new Tesla Roadster will include ~10 small rocket thrusters arranged seamlessly around car." The engines would improve speed and braking, and may "even allow a Tesla to fly."
Tesla started taking $50,000 deposits in 2017, but has since missed every targeted delivery date. As recently as last October, Musk was hyping a Roadster demo that he hoped would happen before the end of 2025. That didn't take place either.
Musk's former friend and OpenAI co-founder Sam Altman mocked the Tesla CEO in posts on X last year over the extreme delays, showing screenshots of his own reservation and refund requests.
"I really was excited for the car! And I understand delays," Altman wrote. "But 7.5 years has felt like a long time to wait."
Altman got his refund, and the two ended up in court earlier this year over a separate matter related to OpenAI's governance and ownership structure.
Others have kept their reservations.
Lawrence O'Connor, founder and CEO of Other World Computing in Austin, Texas, told CNBC ahead of the event that he reserved a Founder's Edition of the new Roadster in November 2017, effectively giving the company what he called an "interest-free loan" of $250,000.
O'Connor wrote in a message that he would be attending the show and was "excited to see what has been 9 years in the making."
According to filings with the Federal Aviation Administration, Tesla established a no-fly zone around the SpaceX facility where it plans to show off the vehicle. The company had to scrap a demo on Oct. 1 due to weather issues.
Tesla is scheduled to report third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday.

articles.title_orig: Australia returns Buddha statute to China amid lasting mystery over its origins
articles.title_zh: Australia returns Buddha statute to China amid lasting mystery over its origins
articles.content_orig:
The Ming dynasty artefact was found buried by the roadside in 2018 and no one can say how it came to arrive in the country
A 500-year-old Buddha statue that was found buried by a roadside in Australia has been returned to China, leaving an ongoing mystery about how it arrived in the country.
The 15cm (six-inch) bronze figurine was formally handed over to Chinese consular representatives during a ceremony in the coastal town of Denham in Shark Bay on Tuesday, the public broadcaster ABC reported.
It will be taken to China for further evaluation to establish its history before being displayed at a museum in Beijing.

articles.title_orig: Houthi Missiles Strike Government Headquarters in Yemen
articles.title_zh: Houthi Missiles Strike Government Headquarters in Yemen
articles.content_orig:
Iran-aligned Houthi rebels carried out a deadly attack on the presidential Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, the headquarters of Yemen’s internationally recognized government, on Thursday, killing five people, including two members of Prime Minister Shaya Al-Zindani’s security detail.
The missile and drone attack also injured 16 people, according to Yemen’s Health Ministry, while the Houthis claimed they were targeting an alleged Saudi military operations center inside the compound.
Yemen’s Health Minister Qasim Mohammed Buhaibeh said the casualties included security personnel and civilian employees working at the government complex, which serves as a key workplace for senior officials including the prime minister.
In a statement posted by the government’s Ministry of Information, officials said the prime minister and members of the government were safe following the attack.
The strike is one of the highest-profile attacks on the Yemeni government since its launch earlier this month of operation “Yemen’s Dawn” — the latest campaign in its long-running war against the rebels.
The internationally recognized government took Aden as its de facto capital after the Houthis seized the official capital, Sanaa, in 2014. Saudi Arabia has since backed the government in its fight against the rebels, in an effort to contain the conflict on its southern border.
The Houthis claimed Thursday’s strike was part of a declared strategy of targeting Saudi military deployments wherever they are located.
“The shelling of the Saudi enemy’s war operations headquarters in Aden comes within the framework of the declared equation of targeting Saudi military build-ups wherever they may be, and considering any military presence of the Saudi enemy a legitimate target for our forces,” the statement said.
The Yemeni government did not immediately provide additional details about the type of missiles used or the extent of the damage at the palace compound.
CNN International Diplomatic Editor Nic Robertson, who has visited the palace twice, most recently in 2019, said the complex sits on a fortified rocky outcrop overlooking Aden and is accessed via a heavily secured road.
In a statement issued later Thursday, Yemen’s Cabinet said the attack involved both missiles and drones, adding that it would not affect the government’s operations or its campaign against the Houthis.
“Yemen’s future will not be held hostage by a militia that bears arms against its own people, targets the security of its neighbors, and relies on violence to compensate for the Yemeni people’s rejection of its coup-driven agenda,” it said.
The attack came less than an hour after Houthi forces renewed warnings that Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe and that they retained the capability to “respond in kind” to ongoing Saudi attacks on Yemen.
The Houthis said Thursday that Saudi Arabia had launched 65 airstrikes and missile attacks across Yemen over the previous 24 hours, targeting Sanaa and several other provinces. Between Sept. 3 and Oct. 15, Saudi airstrikes and missile attacks had killed 120 people and wounded 307 others, the Health Ministry said — claiming that women and children accounted for about 60% of the casualties. CNN cannot independently verify the figures.
Meanwhile, Yemen’s military said Thursday that it had killed a prominent Houthi commander known as “Abu al-Fadl al-Hadrami,” describing him as the head of the group’s ballistic missile and drone operations and one of its most senior military figures. The military said Al-Hadrami had undergone specialized training in Iran — a claim CNN cannot independently verify.
Experts say the Saudi-led coalition’s targeting of senior Houthi military figures in recent weeks raises questions about whether the attack on the palace was intended to signal the Houthis’ ability to respond by striking senior government officials despite the intensified military pressure on them.
The Saudi-led coalition said Thursday that recent Houthi attacks , including strikes targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, demonstrate the growing threat posed by the Iran-aligned group to Saudi Arabia, regional security and international shipping routes.
The coalition’s spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said the rebels have acquired “advanced technologies” with support from regional actors and become “the first terrorist group to possess ballistic missiles, offensive and suicide drones, and booby-trapped fast boats.”
The coalition also said military operations would continue with the aim of degrading Houthi military capabilities and removing sources of support for the group’s war effort in accordance with international humanitarian law.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have been escalating in recent days. On Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed multiple aerial threats across the kingdom, including a drone over Khamis Mushait in southwestern Saudi Arabia, a cruise missile over the Medina region in the west, and another drone in the Eastern Province.
Why billions spent on defense haven’t shielded Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
The attacks have raised concerns about energy supplies, commercial shipping and fuel prices, with the Houthis increasingly targeting Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and maritime traffic.
Earlier this week, US President Donald Trump accused the Houthis of trying to drive up oil prices and suggested Iran was encouraging the group’s latest attacks.
“The Houthis are behaving very badly,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “They’ve been silent for a long time, but now they’ve emerged again, probably at the behest of Iran … hitting Saudi Arabia, and purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices, probably prior to the US elections .”

articles.title_orig: Two new cases of New World screwworm identified in New Mexico
articles.title_zh: Two new cases of New World screwworm identified in New Mexico
articles.content_orig:
Cornelio Salazar unties baler twine as the Salazar brothers feed their 250 cattle in April at their 3,000-acre USA Ranch in Cañones. For ranchers, whose herds are susceptible to New World screwworm infestations, the flies pose just one more challenge in a year full of challenges.
Two new cases of New World screwworm have been identified in Grant County, state and federal agriculture officials announced Thursday evening.
One infestation was found in a horse and the other in a calf.
The cases are New Mexico's third and fourth since the sometimes-deadly pest made its return to the United States this summer, after being largely eradicated from the nation decades earlier. Previous cases in New Mexico were found in a Lea County dog and a Grant County horse .
“We are working closely with our state and federal partners to investigate these cases, increase surveillance and monitor for additional infestations,” State Veterinarian Samantha Holeck said in a statement.
Livestock officials have established an “infested zone” with a radius of at least 12.4 miles around each of the animals’ locations. Within these zones, animals must be inspected and, if necessary, treated before being moved within or out of the area.
The New Mexico Department of Agriculture advised animal owners to closely monitor their critters for wounds that fail to heal, worsening injuries, foul-smelling discharge or unusual irritation. Anyone who suspects an animal may have a New World screwworm infestation should contact the New Mexico Livestock Board and avoid moving the animal.
“We appreciate the continued cooperation of livestock producers, veterinarians and animal owners as we respond to these additional cases,” New Mexico Agriculture Secretary Jeff Witte said in a statement. “Early detection and prompt reporting are critical to limiting the spread of this pest. We encourage everyone to remain vigilant and work closely with animal health officials.”
Common in the Caribbean and Central America, the New World screwworm flies’ larvae burrow into the flesh of warm-blooded creatures such as livestock, pets, wildlife and, in rare cases, people, causing painful and putrid wounds.
The pest, effectively eliminated from the U.S. in the 1960s, crossed the U.S.-Mexico border in June. The U.S. Department of Agriculture has since identified 55 animal infestations across New Mexico and Texas, including the two new cases in Grant County.
Hundreds of other cases are active in the Mexican border states of Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas.
To combat the pest, the U.S. Department of Agriculture has greatly increased efforts to breed and disperse sterile screwworm flies, which can’t produce the larvae that would be harmful.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, meanwhile, has issued emergency-use authorizations for medications to prevent and treat New World screwworm infestations in cattle, sheep, goats, horses, birds, dogs and cats.
Margaret O'Hara reports on issues affecting healthy communities in New Mexico. Her work is funded by a grant from Anchorum Health Foundation. Anchorum will not have any role in editorial decisions. articles.title_orig: FINISHING ON TOP OF THE WORLD
articles.title_zh: FINISHING ON TOP OF THE WORLD
articles.content_orig:
There has been no shortage of drama since Laver Cup London 2026, with Team Europe’s Carlos Alcaraz rediscovering the joy of winning, and Alexander Zverev reaching a career-defining milestone as he prepares to become world No. 1.
After helping Team Europe secure its sixth Laver Cup title at The O2, both stars carried their momentum into the Asian swing, setting up an intriguing finish to the 2026 season.
Carlos Alcaraz’s return from a wrist injury gained momentum in London. After reaching the US Open quarterfinals, the Spaniard delivered two victories for Team Europe, winning both his singles and doubles matches as captain Yannick Noah and vice-captain Tim Henman guided the blue team to victory.
For Alcaraz, representing Europe provided another reminder of the enjoyment he finds in competing alongside his teammates. “These kind of weeks help me a lot to bring my joy back on the court, bring my joy back on playing tennis, and helps me a lot for the next tournaments when it is not team events,” Alcaraz said at The O2 in September.
That winning feeling followed him to Tokyo, where the 23-year-old successfully defended his ATP 500 title. It was his first tournament triumph since returning from injury and his first since lifting the trophy in Qatar in February.
“I didn’t know if I was going to win a tournament this soon or if I was going to win a tournament this season,” he said.
“Everything I’ve done to be in this position, everything I’ve worked for, for this moment, it feels even more special.”
The Tokyo victory was Alcaraz’s third title of the season and the 27th of his career. He arrived in Shanghai for his first ATP Masters 1000 appearance since returning from injury, sporting a new mustache and infectious positivity. “I always wanted to step on the court at least once with the mustache,” Alcaraz beamed.
“So, before Tokyo, it was, it was like, ‘Alright, if I win the tournament, we all have to do the mustache’.” His Shanghai campaign ended in the third round, but the Tokyo title marked an important step in his return to competition as he looks ahead to the final tournaments of the season.
Meanwhile, Zverev has secured one of the biggest milestones of his career. Next month the German will become the 30 th member of the No. 1 Club and officially finish the year as world No.1. He has ended the season inside the Top 10 of the year-end PIF ATP Rankings eight times, including five finishes inside the Top.5. It will be the first time he finishes the year at the top.
“It’s been a fantastic season for me winning in Paris and New York and knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true,” Zverev said. “So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal, especially after coming back from the ankle injury. I look forward to finishing the season in style.”
Speaking to ATP.com in London, Team Europe captain Yannick Noah heaped praised on Zverev’s resilience and persistence to reach the top. “He’s been searching for it for so long, and it’s very inspiring to see a player being so close for so many years and never giving up,” Noah said. “All of a sudden, he had this little opening this year, and he was ready. He took it, and he deserves it.”
Added vice-captain Tim Henman: “A lot of it is about game style, strategy and confidence. I think 12 months ago, Sascha was low on all of them. But when you see the way he’s been stepping up in the big matches, he hasn’t always played his best, but he’s found a way to win. Then you give yourself a chance to play better. The way he’s played in the Slams speaks for itself.”
Zverev is also chasing his first Shanghai title and ninth ATP Masters 1000 crown. He arrived in Shanghai as the top seed and recorded his 60th tour-level victory of the season with a third-round win over Quentin Halys, matching his tally from 2018 putting him in reach of the 69 victories he recorded in 2024.
Zverev’s achievements extend to Laver Cup, where he became a six-time champion and the highest-scoring player in the competition’s history, with 26 points. He also leads the race to Turin, where the season-ending ATP Finals will bring together the top eight players in the PIF ATP Rankings from November 15–22.
Alcaraz has already qualified, while Alex de Minaur (10 th place) is among those chasing a place along with Rafael Jodar (11 th ), both quarterfinalists in Shanghai. The Australian reached the final in Beijing before continuing his campaign in Shanghai, where he overcame an injury concern to progress.

articles.title_orig: Authorities investigate letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to congressional, election offices
articles.title_zh: Authorities investigate letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to congressional, election offices
articles.content_orig:
Federal authorities say they are investigating "potentially hazardous" letters containing "suspicious substances" that have been sent to congressional and state election offices around the US.
The FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) said they were trying to trace the "suspicious mailings", some of which were intercepted before they were received.
Authorities declined to say how many offices had been targeted, but several secretaries of state and congressional offices reported receiving the letters.
Coming just weeks before the US midterm elections, it echoes previous security scares involving suspicious mail.
The suspicious letters were sent to at least five Democratic senators' offices, most of which were intercepted before delivery.
They include California's Alex Padilla, Connecticut's Chris Murphy and New York's Kirsten Gillibrand, the senators' offices confirmed to the BBC.
New York Senator Chuck Schumer and Delaware Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester were also sent the suspicious pieces of mail, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.
"This incident is a stark reminder of the very real danger facing those who serve the public and who help administer our elections in the face of increasingly hostile political rhetoric," Padilla said in a statement to the BBC.
Several state offices have also received the suspicious mailings.
Delaware's Department of Elections said its office received and opened a letter containing a white powdery substance on Thursday, adding that staff followed security protocols on handling suspicious mail.
The Oklahoma State Election Board and the Louisiana secretary of state both said this week that their offices had received letters containing a white powder.
The Louisiana office was evacuated after a staff member opened the package on Tuesday, but it has since reopened after law enforcement found no evidence of harmful substances.
Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose said his office was the intended recipient of a letter containing white powder, but the USPIS had intercepted it.
The New York State Capitol in Albany and the Wyoming State Capitol in Cheyenne also received suspicious packages, according to emergency responder scanner feed reviewed by the BBC.
"This FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service will continue to safeguard the public and secure elections for American citizens," the agencies said in a statement on Thursday.
The suspicious mailings come just weeks before election day, which will determine the balance of power in Congress.
Ahead of the 2024 election, vote officials in 17 states received suspicious packages .
A year earlier, suspicious envelopes, some laced with fentanyl, were sent to election offices in at least five states.

articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Order to limit Starshield for Ukraine came from inside White House, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Bones were discovered outside the so-called house of horrors in the Olney section of Philadelphia, but it's unclear whether they are related to the ongoing investigation into Raymond "R.C." Horsch, a suspected serial killer who died last year, sources told CBS News Philadelphia on Thursday.
The Philadelphia Medical Examiner's Office responded to the house at 417 West Chew Ave. on Thursday, sources close to the investigation confirmed.
The bones were found in the backyard, where agents and detectives have been painstakingly searching for any sign of human remains and any evidence of at least seven women connected to Horsch and the house, some of whom are feared dead, sources told CBS News Philadelphia.
It's not clear whether they were human or animal bones, sources stressed. More testing is needed to determine the bones' origin and whether they are connected to the investigation.
Richard Marx, a retired FBI supervisory agent who specialized in evidence collection, said the presence of the medical examiner is a significant development.
"If they find something related to the body, then that's when they would want to call the medical examiner, bring them aboard, have them collect it, and have them take it to their office for examination," Marx said.
Investigators have been methodically sifting through the soil in layers, going down about 3 feet.
Investigators found human DNA when they used luminol to search the home, police sources confirmed earlier this week.
A source also said investigators had found opossum carcasses near the house. The remnants of a brick outhouse were also uncovered in the yard.
The investigation at the house is expected to continue until at least the middle of next week, sources said. Investigators are set to dig up the front yard when they are finished in the back.
Investigators believe Horsch used a process known as alkaline hydrolysis to dispose of bodies , law enforcement sources said. He detailed the steps in one of his books in which he called himself an empathetic serial killer. Chemicals found in the home have been sent to laboratories for testing.
Before his death, Horsch lived in the house with his son, Eugene , whose arrest during a traffic stop in June kicked off this massive investigation.
Stay with CBS News Philadelphia for ongoing coverage of this investigation and follow on YouTube for extended "House of Horrors" coverage every Friday .

articles.title_orig: Jon Gosselin Warns Those Making ‘False Claims’ About Son Collin After Ex Kate’s ‘Mental Illness’ Remark
articles.title_zh: Jon Gosselin Warns Those Making ‘False Claims’ About Son Collin After Ex Kate’s ‘Mental Illness’ Remark
articles.content_orig:
Jon Gosselin is coming to his son's defense.
After the October 13 release of Collin Gosselin 's memoir, In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood — in which he accused his mother , Kate Gosselin , of abusing him as a child — Jon, 49, spoke out both to congratulate his 22-year-old son on the book and to support him.
"First and foremost, I couldn't be more proud of my son's heartbreaking memoir and his mission to help other victims of abuse," Jon told Us Weekly in a statement on Thursday, October 15.
Jon, who shares twin daughters and sextuplets with the Jon & Kate Plus 8 alum, 51, also appeared to respond to Kate's recent remarks, in which she seemingly claimed Collin suffered from mental illness.
"Also, let me be very clear: If you continue to falsely label my son Collin as 'mentally ill,' you will be held accountable," he continued. "As you know, Collin has been evaluated by multiple independent psychiatrists, and that narrative is proven categorically untrue."
"Repeating false claims about his mental health is damaging to his reputation, his credibility and his future," Jon maintained. "Consider this fair warning: The days of using mental health to discredit and silence my son are over."
While Jon didn't name Kate directly in his statement to the outlet, his comments come after Kate appeared to address Collin's "mental illness" in an October 10 comment on her TikTok .
In response to a fan who told Kate she was "doing a great job keeping [her] head up" amid Collin's tell-all book, the former TV personality wrote, "I know rational logical [people] or anyone who has dealt with mental illness understands what's going on here. I had nothing to do with it."
Kate has long denied allegations of abuse against Collin, with her attorney telling The U.S. Sun in 2024 that he didn't believe she had done anything to "intentionally harm" Collin.
He also said "she did what she did to protect herself and her family" from what he called Collin's "troubled behavior."
Previously addressing Collin's new book , Kate responded to a follower in the comment section of a June 2026 TikTok video who suggested she sue her son for defamation if his accusations were false.
"If you are 100% certain that the accusations against you are lies, my suggestion would be to take him to court and sue him for defamation!" the follower wrote.
"I can't bc I'm a public figure," Kate replied at the time. "Rules are different unfortunately. Or I def would!"

articles.title_orig: Tesla Roadster Reveal Dents TSLA Stock 4% [2026]
articles.title_zh: Tesla Roadster Reveal Dents TSLA Stock 4% [2026]
articles.content_orig:
The next-gen Roadster has been in development for nearly a decade. But perhaps it was worth the wait.
The next-gen Roadster has been in development for nearly a decade. But perhaps it was worth the wait.
Elon Musk promised a flying car. And the Tesla Roadster did exactly that.
Tesla demonstrated its next-generation Roadster at an event in Waco, Texas, where the electric supercar drove upside down, briefly flew, and accelerated to 60mph in under a second. It was an impressive demonstration of a car that likely will come with some heavy caveats if it ever goes into production.
The event was less than 30 minutes and felt more like a stunt show than a product reveal. Indeed, there was no mention of price, trim levels, or other such mundane details. Who cares about that boring crap anyway? The people were here to see a car fly, and that’s what Tesla gave them.
The next-gen Roadster certainly took the scenic route in getting here. A prototype version was announced as a “one more thing” style surprise during the 2017 Tesla Semi event . The specs sounded ludicrous even back then: 0-60 mph in 1.9 seconds, a top speed over 250 mph, a 200 kWh battery delivering up to 620 miles of range, and a $200,000 starting price tag. Musk said deliveries would start in 2020, which sounded perfectly doable at the time.
Early adopters quickly threw down $50,000 deposits (or $250,000 for the limited Founders Series), effectively interest-free loans to help fund Tesla’s scaling ambitions. But then Tesla seemed to forget about the Roadster, as cementing its status as the ultimate vaporware . Production deadlines slipped as Tesla prioritized mass-market vehicles like the Model Y, while also wrestling with the overly complicated Cybertruck. Occasionally, when Musk would remember that the Roadster existed, he would up the ante about its capabilities. This culminated in the “SpaceX package” that would equip the supercar with cold-gas thrusters, bestowing hover powers and a 0-60 time under one second.
Musk has also sought to downplay the Roadster’s significance, calling it a “small potato situation” that will not “move the needle in a major way financially.” He’s framed the supercar more as a joint engineering collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, even questioning whether it’s “even a car anymore” given its experimental nature. Some analysts theorize that the decision to re-release the Roadster is an attempt to set the stage for a rumored Tesla-SpaceX merger .
Tesla’s failure to bring the Roadster to market allowed other automakers to slip passed the company with their own hyper-powered EVs. Rimac has smashed performance records with the Nevera, Porsche has refined electric performance with the Taycan, and Chinese giants like BYD are producing track-ready supercars at a fraction of the cost. The Roadster is no longer shocking the world as an impossible prototype; it’s playing catch-up to an industry that spent nine years building what Tesla merely rendered.

articles.title_orig: Measles cases reach 42 in rural Minnesota amid outbreaks
articles.title_zh: Measles cases reach 42 in rural Minnesota amid outbreaks
articles.content_orig:
The Minnesota Department of Health says it has identified two separate measles outbreaks in southeastern and central Minnesota, leaded to 25 cases in the last month.
The clusters in Fillmore and Todd counties in recent weeks make up more than half of the measles cases in Minnesota this year. According to the state's department of health, all the people who got sick were unvaccinated.
Measles, which was eliminated in the U.S. for decades, is classified by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention as one of the most contagious infectious diseases. The best way to prevent the disease is through vaccination, the department of health says.
"There are pockets of unvaccinated or under-vaccinated people across Minnesota, and anyone who isn't vaccinated against measles is at risk, especially right now," the health department said in a statement.
Overall, the U.S. has seen 4,000 cases of measles this year. Forty-two of those cases have happened in Minnesota. Last year, Minnesota saw 26 total cases.

articles.title_orig: ICE Agents Who Rammed a Worker in Houston Were Chasing a Dead Man, Family Says
articles.title_zh: ICE Agents Who Rammed a Worker in Houston Were Chasing a Dead Man, Family Says
articles.content_orig:
HOUSTON — Videos collected by local investigators make it "pretty obvious" that an ICE officer intentionally ran over Miguel Parra Hernandez during an immigration stop Saturday, which could lead to assault charges, the district attorney said Tuesday.
"This was an intentional striking and running over of the person by the vehicle, and in that case, that is an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon in Texas," Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare told NBC News.
Teare said the federal government is not cooperating with the investigation conducted by his office and the Harris County Sheriff's Office. He also said ICE may have allowed the erasure of critical data in the vehicle involved in striking Parra, who was on foot.
Teare said that in his seven years as a Harris County vehicular crimes division chief, he has reviewed video from a number of other auto-pedestrian collision cases. He said the video his investigators have gathered in Parra's case "goes above" the video that was posted online and obtained by NBC affiliate KPRC of Houston.
"My viewing of it, and many other investigators that have viewed it, as well, it's pretty obvious that this was an intentional striking and running over of the person by the vehicle, and in that case, that is an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon in Texas," he said.
Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare. (Raquel Natalicchio / Houston Chronicle via Getty)
Parra, 48, was left with multiple breaks and fractures in his body, according to his attorney and an advocate who has been speaking on his behalf. He had surgery on one leg and faces multiple additional operations, said Cesar Espinosa, co-founder and executive director of FIEL, an immigrant civil rights group.
Video obtained by KPRC shows a white truck headed in the opposite direction of traffic on a busy roadway. It shows a vehicle jumping a yellow median and heading in the direction that Parra is running.
It then appears to show the vehicle, which is not marked, swerving left toward Parra's path, in front of a truck stopped in a shopping center. The parked truck leaves, and a man can be seen on the pavement behind the ICE vehicle, the video shows.
An ICE spokesman said over the weekend that officers were pursuing the fleeing men and that "Miguel Parra Hernandez ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck."
Teare, a Democrat, announced late Monday that his office had launched an independent investigation.
On Tuesday, an ICE spokesperson who was not identified said in a statement that "allegations that ICE struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are RECKLESS and FALSE. The men and women of ICE are entrusted with upholding the rule of law and are held to the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, and ethical conduct."
ICE said the allegations are "disgusting smears" that are "peddled by the media," leading to more than a 1,600% increase in assaults and a 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks against its law enforcement officers. It did not offer data behind those numbers.
ICE has said that Parra was not the target of the attempted stop but that he was in the country illegally. Parra's attorney and family have said he has no criminal record and was on his way to work applying stucco.
Teare said his office and the sheriff's office determined that the vehicle that struck Parra was a Jeep Cherokee and that it potentially had evidence, including a data crash recorder. He said his office wanted to know whether the vehicle locked in information at the time of the collision that could be downloaded, such as speed, steering and braking. Teare said the way to preserve data from the car would have been to "put it on a flatbed trailer and you take it to forensically download it."
But he said he believes any data on the recorder related to the incident could have been erased when ICE drove the car away.
He and the sheriff's investigators told ICE the information needed to be downloaded, but ICE refused, Teare said.
ICE did not respond to questions about a data crash recorder, the erasing of any potential data or any refusal to download it.
"Our office began drafting a search warrant that we were in the process of drafting when the ICE agent in question, the one that had been driving, we believed, at the time of the collision, jumped back into the car and drove it away from the scene," Teare said. "In my 20-year career, I've never heard of anything like that."
Teare also said two people from "an entirely different operation" were in the back seat of the ICE vehicle when it struck Parra. Those two people are also in ICE custody, along with Parra. Teare said his office is working to ensure all three remain in the country as material witnesses.
"I've taught for years at the Houston Police Department Academy, Harris County Department Academy. I've worked with law enforcement for 20 years. There is not a single agency in the United States that would teach that once you put people in custody in your car, you then begin to pursue other people," he said.
Doing so puts "every single person out there in danger again," he said.
According to Teare, the ICE vehicle should have activated its emergency equipment, such as its lights and siren, as it jumped a median and crossed into oncoming traffic.
A senior official at the Department of Homeland Security told NBC News on Tuesday that multiple ICE officers on the scene at the time were wearing body cameras. ICE is reviewing video of the scene as part of an internal investigation, the official said.
Espinosa said Parra told him that he fled because it was unclear whether there were officials in the vehicles, which he said were unmarked, did not use sirens and had dark, tinted windows.
ICE has said it was targeting another man, Jose Mendoza Cervantes, who was in the country illegally and had committed several crimes. Espinoza and Parra's attorney Kim Bruno said neither Parra nor the man who was with him when ICE stopped their vehicle has any association with Mendoza.
Miguel Parra Hernandez. (Noticias Telemundo)
In previous encounters between ICE and targets of its arrests in vehicle stops, including some who have been killed, such as Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston , ICE has alleged the people it tried to arrest weaponized their vehicles .
Parra was struck less than two weeks after the Trump administration issued guidance setting tighter rules for vehicle stops.
The guidance says only agents who have completed specific training should make vehicle stops. The memo also says that vehicles used for traffic stops must have lights and sirens and that all officers on the scenes of vehicle stops must wear and activate their body cameras.
The Harris County District Attorney's Office has been asking witnesses and people who may have photos or video of the incident to contact it. Teare said that there is a secure portal that goes directly to the district attorney's office and that no one is asked about citizenship or immigration status.
"All we are interested in is getting the truth, and any shred of cellphone footage, anyone that saw something and really can point us in the right direction, it would be wonderful," he said.
This article was originally published on NBCNews.com

articles.title_orig: KDE turns 30 with Plasma 6.8, remote upgrades, and an X11 farewell
articles.title_zh: KDE turns 30 with Plasma 6.8, remote upgrades, and an X11 farewell
articles.content_orig:
Marking the 30th anniversary of software developer KDE on October 14, the company released Plasma 6.8, debuted a movie, and retired Plasma’s native X11 session support. The announcement from KDE dubs the new Plasma 6.8 as the “30th Anniversary Edition” and describes the update as preparing Plasma for the future. Legacy X11 applications will still function via the XWayland compatibility layer , and KDE applications will also continue supporting X11 under other desktop environments.
After 42 years in service, the X11 protocol is losing another major desktop environment. Plasma will fully adopt the Wayland system and put support for starting new X11 sessions in Plasma to bed. Users opting to stay on Plasma 6.7 will keep their existing sessions for now. The move was expected, with GNOME officially dropping X11 sessions by default in 2025 .
The new Plasma 6.8 brings many improvements, including increased support for adding window decorations (like shadows and rounded corners) to third-party apps, and a more streamlined Union theming system . Other notable additions include Nvidia triple buffering being enabled by default, Kup backup integration (KDE’s backup utility—now integrated into Plasma), and kscreenctl , a command-line utility that allows power users to adjust display configurations.
An updated System Monitor gives KDE users more control over their system processes, too. The revamped monitor allows users to pin processes directly to CPU cores through the GUI.
Homelabbers should find plenty to be excited about in the release. KDE revamped Plasma’s built-in remote desktop server to cater to clients accessing virtual displays across a network. Highlighted new features include clipboard synchronization between client and server, “ Exclusive Mode ” that locks the server’s physical display and allows the client to set a virtual one that matches their PC, and adaptive remote streaming that aids stability on slower networks.
Linux enthusiasts can also check out a new movie released alongside Plasma 6.8. The KDE team debuted The KDE Documentary — A Story of Free Software Underdogs . An amusing opening-minute interview montage features KDE contributors laughing as they struggle to answer the question “What is KDE?”

articles.title_orig: Rubio urges Lebanon to resist Hezbollah pressure over seized explosives
articles.title_zh: Rubio urges Lebanon to resist Hezbollah pressure over seized explosives
articles.content_orig:
Recent interceptions of weapons and military-grade explosives along the Syrian-Lebanese border highlight Hizbullah's apparent efforts to restore military capabilities weakened by sustained Israeli operations. The reported attempt to smuggle approximately 800 kilograms of C4 and TNT suggests a shift toward acquiring versatile explosive materials that can support decentralized weapons production and defensive preparations. Although these materials could also be used in internal Lebanese confrontations, preparations for renewed hostilities with Israel emerge as a central strategic interpretation. Increased Lebanese and Syrian border enforcement further complicates Hizbullah's efforts to rebuild its military infrastructure and sustain operational readiness.
Over the past two months (August through September 2026, extending into early October), security forces on both sides of the Lebanese-Syrian border have reported multiple specific operations targeting cross-border weapons smuggling.
Early August 2026 (Tartus/Western Syria): Syrian security forces intercepted and foiled an operation attempting to smuggle a significant weapons and ammunition shipment from Tartus toward the Lebanese border. The seized materials included automatic rifles, RPG rounds, weapons magazines, and assorted ammunition.
Arsal Outskirts: The Lebanese Army announced the seizure of a cache of 122 mm Grad rockets that had been smuggled across the mountainous outskirts near Arsal. The military seized the transport vehicle and arrested two individuals tied to the network.
October 7, 2026 (Arsal Border Region): The Lebanese Armed Forces publicly reported foiling another distinct cross-border smuggling operation in the Arsal region amid heightened, exceptional security measures implemented to lock down and monitor the frontier. In parallel, a Lebanese army checkpoint on the road from Damascus to Beirut in the Dahr el Baydar pass foiled an attempt by two members of Hizbullah to introduce almost a ton of C4 and TNT military-grade explosives to Lebanon.
Beyond these official announcements, regional security monitors note that routine skirmishes and smaller tactical seizures occur regularly along rugged, porous stretches of the Anti-Lebanon mountains. However, state authorities rarely break them down into a cumulative public tally.
Why this sudden need for explosives? Is Hizbullah’s short of explosives? Were the explosives meant for a possible operation against governmental officials? Is this signaling that Hizbullah’s is preparing for an internal confrontation in Lebanon or preparations for a renewed conflict with Israel?
These border interceptions highlight a significant tactical shift in Hizbullah’s operational posture and supply lines. The movement of raw explosives like C4 and TNT across the Syrian border into Lebanon, coupled with the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) actively interdicting them, reflects several underlying strategic factors currently shaping Hizbullah’s internal and regional calculus.
Extensive Israeli air campaigns targeting underground Hizbullah infrastructure in the Bekaa Valley, Southern Lebanon, and the Dahiyeh suburb of Beirut have destroyed significant stockpiles of pre-stored munitions, forcing the group to rapidly attempt replenishment via smuggling routes along the porous Syrian border. Indeed, following continuous Israeli strikes against weapons depots and smuggling routes over the past two years, Hizbullah’s traditional, heavy logistics pipelines, particularly for hardened military-grade munitions and factory-made missiles, have experienced severe disruption.
In military terminology, high explosives like C4 and TNT serve as multipurpose “raw material.” Rather than attempting to move bulky, easily detectable completed weapon systems, bringing in concentrated explosives allows local cells to fabricate improvised explosive devices, roadside charges, and anti-armor munitions locally in small, decentralized workshops. High-value explosives like C4 are lightweight, highly stable, malleable, and devastatingly energetic. They are preferred for warfare scenarios where heavy artillery or armored units are unavailable or impractical.
The influx of military-grade plastic explosives and TNT does not necessarily indicate Hizbullah is completely out of munitions, but rather that its supply distribution mechanism has been forced to adapt. C4 offers maximum flexibility since it can be used to manufacture localized weapons against external forces, build roadside IEDs, or maintain a covert sabotage capability for internal domestic control if political and military pressure inside Lebanon escalates further.
However, trying to smuggle 800 kilos of explosives suggests Hizbullah is in the midst of military preparations. That volume is vastly beyond what is needed for targeted assassinations or precision strikes. In military terms, nearly a ton of plastic explosive represents a battalion-level operational capability.
The strategic implications of moving bulk explosive payloads at this scale point to several specific combat preparations:
Against heavily armored forces, high-yield plastic explosives are primarily used to construct massive anti-armor shaped charges, deeply buried roadside charges, and subterranean explosive traps. Standard military protocol for subterranean or fortified defense requires hundreds of kilograms of plastic explosives wired to trigger charges. These can instantly collapse ridgelines, bypass roads, or choke points ahead of advancing armor. Moreover, modern Active Protection Systems (like the Rafael-Elta Trophy Active Protection System)) intercept incoming anti-tank missiles, but they cannot stop a multi-hundred-kilogram buried blast charge that destroys an armored vehicle from underneath using sheer kinetic and blast energy.
If Hizbullah is anticipating a serious internal push from rival militias, the Lebanese Armed Forces, or external ground incursions, 800 kilograms allows for the systemic booby-trapping of entire urban sectors, command bunkers, or logistics hubs. Explosives in these volumes are routinely earmarked to destroy key tactical infrastructure, bridges, access roads, and narrow mountain passes, choking movement and isolating operational sectors.
Because precision-guided missiles and factory-built weapons by Hizbullah are increasingly intercepted before reaching Lebanon, raw C4 is used as a foundational building block for localized arms production. 800 kilos of C4 can produce hundreds of heavy improvised mortar shells, drone warheads, anti-fortification charges, or specialized anti-wall breaching charges for infantry units operating in decentralized cells.
Moving loads near one ton confirms that Hizbullah is not merely engaging in covert cell maintenance; it is actively trying to rebuild structural combat capacity and stockpile bulk ordnance despite intense border monitoring. Whether for subterranean defense along traditional battle lines or for fortified positions in an internal confrontation, a shipment of this magnitude underscores that the organization is bracing for sustained, high-intensity conflict rather than limited covert actions.
Is this a preparation for renewed military confrontation with Israel?
So it seems. A renewed, sustained military confrontation with Israel is the primary strategic driver behind moving high explosives at this scale. While internal signaling and domestic power dynamics are secondary factors, the operational nature of bulk plastic explosives (C4, TNT) aligns directly with the tactical demands of waging a high-intensity campaign against the Israel Defense Forces. These logistics point toward Israel as the primary target for several reasons: In traditional doctrine, bulk military-grade explosives are the essential building blocks for static defense against heavy armor and infantry. articles.title_orig: Trump cancels Hegseth’s plan to live-stream Fort Hood shooter’s execution
articles.title_zh: Trump cancels Hegseth’s plan to live-stream Fort Hood shooter’s execution
articles.content_orig:
SALT LAKE CITY — Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, praised the announcement Thursday from President Donald Trump that the execution of the Fort Hood gunman would no longer be livestreamed.
"This is the right move, both for the loved ones of the victims and for the country," he said in a statement.
The senator was one of several Republicans to push back on last week's announcement that the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan would be publicly streamed, urging Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to "reconsider."
The Pentagon had planned to execute Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist who killed 13 and wounded dozens more in a shooting at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009, publicly on Dec. 3 in what would have been the first legally sanctioned public execution in the nation in 90 years.
"A civilization erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment," Curtis said last week. "Secretary Hegseth's plan to livestream the Fort Hood execution risks feeding that appetite. The victims deserve justice administered with solemnity. Broadcasting a death diminishes us and is not an effective deterrent."
Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson also weighed in last week, calling the plan "deeply disturbing."
Hegseth had argued that the public nature of the execution would serve as a deterrent to future crimes.
"We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public," he said last week. "Because people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things."
Several other Republicans had pushed back on the proposal, and Vice President JD Vance expressed doubts about it last week.
Trump announced Thursday that the execution would proceed in December as planned, but it would not be streamed .
"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," he wrote. "That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!"

articles.title_orig: New York City Comptroller Defends Decision Not to Invest in Israeli Bonds
articles.title_zh: New York City Comptroller Defends Decision Not to Invest in Israeli Bonds
articles.content_orig:
Get the best experience and stay connected to your community with our Spectrum News app. Learn More
New York City Comptroller Mark Levine is walking back his campaign pledge to invest city pension funds in Israel bonds, saying the decision came down to financial returns.
In an interview with The New York Times , Levine said the decision was not politically motivated, though he acknowledged struggling with it on a personal level.
“I always said this would be based on financial considerations only, not politics — that's still my position,” Levine told the Times. “But as of now, we feel that because of some technical challenges, and because of financial considerations, that this is not an investment that we can make right now.”
During his campaign, Levine vowed to purchase Israel bonds after his predecessor, Brad Lander, opted not to renew the investments in 2023.
The Times reported that Israel bonds have returned around 5% on two- and three-year investments, and their technical ratings remain below levels from early 2023.
Levine’s decision has disappointed some Jewish leaders across the city, including former Comptroller Scott Stringer, who invested millions of dollars in Israel bonds during his tenure.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he supports Levine’s decision during a separate news conference.
“I don't believe that our city should purchase Israel bonds, we don't purchase the bonds of any other sovereign nation, I don't think we should make an exception when it comes to Israel,” Mamdani said. “And also, this is the decision that the comptroller is making and it's one that I support.”
When asked by The New York Times why he made the campaign pledge, Levine said he did not have a full understanding of the financial picture.

articles.title_orig: It’s Halloween season at Witchy Woman World Apothecary
articles.title_zh: It’s Halloween season at Witchy Woman World Apothecary
articles.content_orig:
This fall, the fragrance of the season at Witchy Woman World Apothecary at 905 Elmwood Ave. is “Night Blooms.” And, like everything shop owner Sara Shaaban crafts in her in-store laboratory, there’s a story behind it.
Shaaban described the Night Blooms theme as “stepping into an enchanted garden into the things that bloom in the dark,” with hints of floral joined by patchouli, oak moss, fir needles and cedar.
“As we move into this darker half of the year, as people we do the opposite of what nature has always asked us to do,” she said. “Nature asks us to slow down and reflect and look within, cozy up, gather with people, eat scrumptious foods and rest during this time. However, this time of year is very full and busy. So this is an opportunity to slow down a bit. For us here in the shop, we encourage this ‘slowing down’ with our seasonal workshops, products, subscription box themes, sound baths and more. Stepping into the shop during this time of year is an invitation to get sexy with it and lean into this delicious season.”
Shaaban explained that, since launching the company six years ago, her mission has always been to create collections around scents that allow her to lean into the kind of storytelling and folklore that she loves.
One example she gave is a popular seasonal scent called “City of the Dead” — a mixture of bergamot, rose, geranium, blood orange, grapefruit, violet leaf, daisy, amber and mint.
This fall fragrance spawned from a family trip to New Orleans and a visit to one of the city’s famed above-ground cemeteries.
“There was a moment with my son where he felt something going on with a particular grave, and he said, ‘We have to leave something for them.’ And I didn’t question it for a second,” Shaaban said. “We noticed a small empty porcelain vase on the grave, and he skipped off to find flowers to put in it. He wanted to leave an offering. And I remember the smell of that moment so clearly. It was of wet gray stone, fresh greenery, cold air, tree blossoms, connection and joy.”
One of the core products of the City of the Dead collection is a popular bath bomb in the shape of a creepy baby doll head, which Shaaban said is a Halloween favorite and has the aroma of “cold wet stone, fresh florals, a slight cool breeze.”
Another mainstay in her fall collection is October Day, a scent inspired by a tradition Shaaban and her husband have with their kids. The week leading up to Halloween (the actual date varies by year depending on schedules), they celebrate October Day, which Shaaban explained is basically a day of “all things October.”
The activities range from pumpkin patch visits to jumping in leaves, overeating apple cider donuts, carving pumpkins, hay rides and spooky movies. The lead up to October Day has even included hand-drawn posters that now live on the inside of their kitchen cabinets.
So what does October Day smell like? Pumpkin oil, vanilla extract, crisp apple, cinnamon, nutmeg, clove, ginger, cedar and neroli with a hint of orange and sandalwood.
Throughout the season, Shaaban hosts a variety of spiritual and spooky in-store events, including two sessions of broom making on Oct. 25 and Nov. 12. Back by popular demand, the workshop is conducted by local artist and “Broomsquire” Kita. Shaaban said these workshops often sell out, but they plan to schedule additional sessions in the coming months.
At workshops, attendees sit at long tables and create their own decorative and bespoke brooms made from broomcorn, which is a tall coarse grass.
“She [Kita] shares with us broom lore and how brooms have been used throughout history across cultures for both magical and mundane purposes,” Shaaban said. “They’re beautiful, and the broomcorn is hand-dyed, and she always brings in gorgeous talismans and items to adorn your broom with. These brooms are both decorative art pieces as well as fully functional brooms. They’re not only intended to cleanse the space but also be symbols of protection, reverence and intentionality.”
From 5 to 9 p.m. Oct. 29, Shaaban will host her annual Halloween Night Market & Costume Soirée complete with costumes, sweets, candlelight and seasonal cocktails and mocktails.
Long before founding her shop, Shaaban said she worked for a soap company where she was rigorously trained and learned about skincare. She said she never thought she’d revisit these skills until starting her own place years later.
“This is how I connect with my own personal magic, and if I am not physically making these items with my hands, then I don’t know what I’m doing here,” she said. “This is the part I love. This is my art form. It’s why everything is made one-by-one, by hand, and I get to share my art with everyone in this sanctuary space that I created. I don’t make things with popularity or sales in mind. I create things that I am personally excited about and that inspire me. This ultimately inspires those who walk through my door.”
Shaaban also noted that one of the focal points of the shop is the Releasing Ritual Table, which is heavily visited by repeat customers and first-timers alike.
At the table, you can write something on a bay leaf that you no longer need, whether it’s a person or a pattern of behavior or something you just would like to shed and be finished with. Then, she explained, you burn the bay leaf, take a few deep breaths, ring the little brass bell and sit for a moment.
“This is a resource that people can use at any time during an event, or just day to day, and people do,” she said. “They then leave the shop a little less heavy, a little less worried and a little more empowered to move forward.”

Dream rock band Fathom travelled roughly 700km across Australia to play nine shows, setting a new Guinness World Record for most concerts performed in 12 hours across multiple cities.

Fathom partnered with a mental health service, Beyond Blue, donating half of the revenue from ticket sales and merchandise.

articles.title_orig: Trump sues California to prevent counting 20,000 voters' ballots
articles.title_zh: Trump sues California to prevent counting 20,000 voters' ballots
articles.content_orig:
DoJ had demanded that LA county confirm citizenship of people on list in thumb drive, but officials refused
US politics live – latest updates
Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms
The US Department of Justice sued California on Thursday, seeking a court order to prevent the state from tabulating certain ballots cast in the midterm elections .
The suit came two days after the department made a specious demand to the state. On Tuesday, the department sent election officials in Los Angeles county a thumb drive with a handwritten password purporting to contain the names of noncitizens registered to vote. The department asked officials to confirm the citizenship of anyone on the list and set aside ballots from those whose status could not be confirmed. It gave the state 48 hours – an extremely narrow window – to take action. It did not provide details on how it came up with the names on the list. In its lawsuit, filed in federal court in the central district of California , the justice department said it had provided the state with more than 20,000 names of likely noncitizens.
The Los Angeles county clerk and recorder, Dean Logan, said his office would not review the list, in part because it didn’t consider the USB drive secure.
“The Department of Justice has not provided the underlying evidence, source, or methodology supporting its assertions that individuals identified in its records are ineligible to vote,” Logan said in a statement. “We cannot withhold or refuse to count ballots based solely on unverified allegations, nor can we disregard the legal requirements governing our election – and we certainly have no authority to act on records that are outside of our jurisdiction.”
In a statement on Wednesday, the California secretary of state, Shirley Weber, a Democrat, said the justice department had not provided the list of voters to her office. “The [justice department’s] relentless efforts to unlawfully gain access to states’ protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections,” Weber said.
Justice department lawyers are asking the court to order the state not to count votes from those it had flagged.
“This Court should enjoin California from presently tabulating vote-by-mail ballots from likely noncitizens in the upcoming federal election until the voter’s citizenship status can be determined,” the lawsuit said. “This Court should order California (1) to set aside vote-by-mail ballots from persons identified by the Federal Government likely to be noncitizens and (2) to independently – or in collaboration with the Federal Government – verify their citizenship status (beyond relying on unverified statements of citizenship necessary to registering) before tabulating their vote-by-mail ballot.”
The request to block tabulation comes amid concerns that Donald Trump and his allies will interfere in the counting of votes in the midterm elections, in which Republicans are expected to lose seats in Congress.
The Trump administration’s methodology for identifying noncitizens has come under scrutiny. Earlier this year, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said there could be as many as 278,000 noncitizens on the rolls in four states, including more than 190,000 in California and about 16,000 in Nevada.
after newsletter promotion
Officials at the DHS refused to share their methodology with Nevada election officials and later turned over just 185 names of people it had a strong belief were noncitizens. When Nevada officials investigated, they found every one of those people was a citizen.
Richard Hasen, an election law scholar at UCLA, described the justice department’s efforts in California as “a nice publicity stunt that gets attention for [the justice department] and reinforces the notion among the president’s most ardent supporters that California is not doing enough to combat voter fraud”.
“The Department of Justice has no standing to tell states and localities to go in and remove voters from voting rolls in the midst of an election. In fact, the National Voter Registration Act bars systematic purges of ineligible voters in the 90-day period before the election,” he wrote in a blogpost . “The purpose of this provision, unsurprisingly, is to stop false positives, that is the removal of eligible voters who are mistakenly flagged as noncitizens. A rushed process would almost certainly lead to disenfranchisement.”

articles.title_orig: Cracks are beginning to show in the stock market as doubts about AI investments grow
articles.title_zh: Cracks are beginning to show in the stock market as doubts about AI investments grow
articles.content_orig:
Just one week after hitting fresh all-time highs, U.S. stocks are showing signs of strain as investors begin to fret about returns on the trillions of dollars that have been put into AI.
For U.S. consumers, it could mean a shakier economy moving forward.
After trading closed Thursday, the S&P 500 was off 1% from its week-ago record, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq had fallen more than 3% below its peak last week.
Driving the declines: Quarterly revenue growth at Anthropic has slowed, the Financial Times reported Wednesday. The AI giant is expected to be worth more than $1 trillion when it goes public, and at nearly $17 billion, its revenue is still massive and the company said it is profitable.
There are also rising concerns about whether China-based memory technology companies could undermine, or even overtake, their Western rivals. And even though the AI data center buildout has created a global shortage of processing chips, there are fears that Chinese mass production of memory chips could flood the market with an oversupply.
Meanwhile, investors have begun selling off the bonds backing some data centers , primarily over fears that AI revenues won’t be sufficient to cover the massive sums that have been borrowed to finance the building of the centers.
On Thursday, economist Ed Yardeni, a widely respected market commentator, lowered his year-end target for the S&P 500 to 7,900, down from 8,400, over what he said was rising investor caution about the artificial intelligence trade and lingering doubts about inflation and higher interest rates. The S&P 500 currently sits at about 7,600.
Most Americans don’t directly own tech stocks, let alone work in AI, which a growing number of studies show may have begun to limit job opportunities. Still, the AI buildout has been a massive part of what’s bolstering the economy, at least on paper.
Nearly half of all U.S. economy growth this year is attributable to tech-related spending . Those investments have also lifted the stock market even as a growing swath of other companies have experienced sharp declines in their share prices.
The tech-driven gains have in turn created a wealth effect that has helped propel steady U.S. consumer spending and, by extension, the job market. The result has been sturdy economic growth, even as lower-income and even middle-income households have continued to struggle under stubborn inflation and declining earnings.
“While higher interest rates, higher oil prices and persistent inflation create risks to the economy, strong positive forces such as the investment in AI infrastructure, high employment levels and consistent wage growth continue to outweigh the risks,” Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf said this week.
But other economists say consumers are already contending with a host of stressors that stand to weaken their position. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Thursday that inflation among businesses reached its highest rate since December 2022 — price growth that could eventually trickle down to consumers.
If tech spending — and stocks — show any sign of sustained declines, broader U.S. economic growth would likely be at risk.
“Higher interest rates, elevated energy prices, slow job growth and the sell-off in equities (if it continues) are all downside risks to consumer spending,” analysts with Citi wrote in a note Thursday.
Rob Wile is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist covering breaking business stories for NBCNews.com.
